note_tweet.text:
I think this is one of the most important graphs of the last few months, and perhaps years. For a long time, there was speculation about how AI would affect the labor market.

Clearly, it was only a matter of time before AI reached the white-collar sector, but empirical evidence was scarce, ultimately because, of course, one only really understands how the market situation develops in retrospect.

Now, as in this example, we see that AI is clearly and unequivocally entering certain professions and replacing people. Call center agents are the first to be replaced. And as more AI and agents enter the workforce, a similar process will spread to other areas of work. Frankly, I don't believe that AI will necessarily create new jobs, resulting in a net zero. I think more jobs will be replaced than created. This needs to be discussed.

note_tweet.text:
Scientists reprogrammed leukemia to switch itself off, and it worked

Researchers at the Institut Pasteur developed a new approach that changes how malignant B-cell leukemia shuts itself down, while also drawing the immune system into action. Most treatments try to remove cancer cells directly, but this method works by triggering a process that sends strong warning signals to immune cells, helping the body recognize and clear the disease. This response normally does not occur in B-cell leukemia because a key molecular component is missing. By combining three clinically used compounds, the researchers were able to work around this limitation and activate the immune response. Using advanced imaging in preclinical models, they observed immune cells rapidly moving in and clearing the leukemia. 

In these experiments, the disease did not just lessen, it was completely cleared. Although this approach has not yet been tested in patients, the findings point to a promising strategy that relies on immune-mediated tumor control, with the potential for faster clinical evaluation because existing compounds were used.

Nearly one in three Indian schools lacked internet access in the 2025–26 academic year.

The Education Ministry’s UDISE+ report recorded internet facilities in 67.4% of schools. It lists 14,66,682 schools nationwide, with internet available in 9,89,191. That leaves 4,77,491 schools without it.

Starlink could help connect remote schools and give teachers and students access to more learning resources. A child’s opportunities should not depend on whether a broadband cable reaches their classroom. 

Starlink has already connected more than 6 million students worldwide. This is another powerful reason to support Starlink in India.
